description:
STEP 1 (build beside the old). Code-review finding 1. This is the heart of fz-hwn.23.

The backend-boundary predicate is OPEN WORK, not a settled fact. A polymorphic template activation reaches the backend and its bare-var value materializes as NativeBoundValue::Absent and panics on use. BUT the exact mechanism is NOT "bare var => empty type": code review verified is_empty requires self.vars.is_none() (descr.rs:412), so a bare var is NOT is_empty. The earlier "bare var => unrepresentable" story is wrong; do not assume the syntactic predicate is correct until a test pins it.

Work: characterize, against REAL native lowering, the exact predicate that excludes precisely the activations that cannot become backend executables.
Candidates:
- is_value_template (a pure var, or a tuple with a bare-var field) -- the cheap, sound, SYNTACTIC approximation (types/mod.rs value_lane_repr returns the bare var unchanged).
- meaningful-variable groundness: mvar(t) = { a in var(t) | t[0/a] != t } -- Castagna, the principled semantic target; escalate to it if the syntactic predicate proves too coarse. Belongs on the calculator side, never the key.

Deliverable: a test that pins which predicate correctly classifies the FunctionId(164)[a0,a0] phantom and its siblings as non-materializable, so re-keying (Step 2) can ground-or-prune exactly those activations.

Depends on: addressed-arrow machinery (fz-hwn.27.2).
Checks: a lowering-level test asserts the predicate against the with_index repro phantom; documents whether is_value_template suffices or mvar is required. Lib green, zero warnings.
title: Pin the backend-boundary value-template predicate by test (is_value_template vs mvar)
